style.vernacular: City of Soviet-era prefabricated panel blocks of 5 (khrushchovka), 9 and 16 storeys in grey concrete or painted cream, yellow and pale blue, with flat bitumen roofs, tiled mosaics and enclosed balconies; Stalinist neoclassical blocks in cream stucco with white pilasters and spires on Khreshchatyk; pre-revolution 3 to 5 storey brick and stucco buildings in pastel ochre, pink and green; white-walled Ukrainian Baroque churches with green roofs and gold domes; post-2000 glass-and-metal towers and malls. Chestnut, linden and maple street trees; pine forest on the outskirts.
style.ornament: Ukrainian Baroque white walls with gold and blue onion domes and green copper roofs; Stalinist neoclassical pilasters, cornices and spires; Art Nouveau stucco (House with Chimaeras); Soviet ceramic mosaic panels and relief friezes on panel blocks; painted-over concrete balconies; Constructivist and brutalist public buildings.

sources.what: landmarks: St Sophia Cathedral, St Andrew church, House with Chimaeras, Red University Building, Khreshchatyk rebuilt after 1941; the palette of panel blocks and pastel stucco is general knowledge of Soviet-era housing
